I’ve attached a preliminary evidence intake form and our internal incident triage checklist. We are not assuming fault; we need a rapid alignment on who holds custody and whether cross-border transit occurred.

Thanks — Samir

Naomi — quick operational update from infra:
- Confirmed an outbound POST to analytics-collect.example.net at 2027-06-29T00:42:14Z from a connector instance provisioned for HS-8842; egress via our data-transfer subprocessor "EdgeStream Analytics" (edge-stream-prod).
- Payload size ~ 14KB; content sniffing (safe-mode) shows JSON with hashed identifiers and one metadata field "encounter_type". No raw SSNs or full patient names detected in the sample.
- We captured flow logs and a memory snapshot of the connector container; snapshots are stored in the incident bucket and accessible to forensics.
- Geo: the destination resolved to a US-based CDN endpoint but traces show a downstream aggregation partner in EU (possible onward transfer).

Next steps I propose:
1) Produce a 1-page summary for Nimbus (destination, subprocessor, sample content types).
2) Prepare a formal evidence package (logs + snapshot) for secure transfer (we need their intake SFTP or a signed upload link).
3) Rishi: confirm whether the connector job was expected to forward to third-party analytics for that account (was it part of pilot config?).

I can have the summary + evidence package ready within 4 hours if legal gives the green light on what we can share now.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] Possible export of PII via integration job — DPA obligations and disclosure scope

Thanks for the fast triage. High-level legal guidance while we assemble artifacts:

1) DPA trigger and timing: our standard DPA (Section 6.2 — Incident Notification) requires us to notify the controller (Nimbus) without undue delay and provide reasonably available information about the nature of the incident. There is not an absolute 72-hour hard stop in our DPA like some controllers insist on, but we should assume Nimbus may need a regulator notification if material personal data is involved.

2) Subprocessor chain: provide the identity of the first-tier subprocessor (EdgeStream Analytics) and describe onward transfer destinations as 'may involve downstream partners' if we cannot materially confirm the EU aggregation partner yet. Avoid naming downstream partners until confirmed by traces. That limits legal risk while giving Nimbus the routing context they requested.

3) Evidence transfer: we can supply logs + memory snapshot under a secured channel (signed S3 presigned with restricted TTL or their SFTP). Attach a Data Transfer Agreement amendment if the transfer will cross borders and they ask us to host evidence in EU. Forensics access should be limited to specified personnel; ask Nimbus to sign our forensic access form (they already attached one — good).

4) Regulator reporting: advise Nimbus we are treating this as a 'possible exposure' and will cooperate fully. Offer a joint statement template (we can draft) to help them with any regulator engagement. If they choose to notify, document the timeline and artifacts we provided (for our records and any follow-up contractual obligations).

5) Customer comms: Jordan, please send Nimbus a concise ETA: initial summary within 3 hours, full evidence package within 6–8 hours contingent on receipt of their signed intake form and destination for evidence. Keep the wording limited to facts and avoid speculation about root cause until post-forensics.

I will draft the short notice language for Nimbus and include the DPA references. We should also confirm whether the pilot terms included any exception for analytics forwarding; Rishi, can you confirm that by EOD?

Lauren Bishop
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
